same-scores-different-worlds.heading: Start here: identical scores, different shared failures
same-scores-different-worlds.synopsis: Move the missed items while both individual scores stay fixed. See why shared misses can range from zero to ten.
limits: The 100 items and their arrangements are constructions, not measurements of a system.
The bounds describe possible shared miss rates; they do not recover the true relationship between real guards.
The independence point is one assumption's answer; the film does not select a point inside the interval or certify safety.

thirteen-worlds.heading: What changes when joint rows are released?
thirteen-worlds.synopsis: One released file allows thirteen counts from separate scores. Its joint rows identify one: nine shared misses among 82 selected items.
limits: These counts describe one selected released subset, not a population rate or a prediction.
Vendor settings are unstated. This does not rank products or cover unreleased adversarial prompts.
Item positions are constructed. Only the displayed aggregate counts come from the release.
The joint rows identify shared misses in this file, not general dependence, causal contribution, or every overlap.

leave-one-out.heading: Which items does only one guard catch?
leave-one-out.synopsis: Which guard catches an item that every other guard misses? Released leave-one-out unions identify exclusive counts of 18, 3, 0, 0, and 0.
limits: These counts describe one selected released subset, not deployed systems or a wider population.
Vendor settings are unstated. This does not rank products or cover unreleased adversarial prompts.
Only aggregate counts come from the release; the positions of items are constructed.
Exclusive coverage is not causal contribution, a Shapley value, or a map of all overlaps.

parity-cube.heading: Can every pair agree while all three differ?
parity-cube.synopsis: Even every pair can agree while the all-three failure rate changes. A synthetic construction exposes what pairwise measurements leave open.
limits: This synthetic E1 construction shows possibility, not the frequency of this pattern in real guardrail stacks.
No real guardrail, vendor, or deployment is measured, and no practical or deployed value of the framework is validated.

the-missing-column-census.heading: Which evaluations preserve joint evidence?
the-missing-column-census.synopsis: Inspect a bounded review of 20 public evaluations: five retain some joint evidence; zero document matched thresholds with full exposure.
limits: An unfilled reporting column does not show poor guardrail performance or establish that the unknown joint statistics would reveal dependence.
The census records reporting fields, not the quality or scores of each per-system evaluation.
Coverage is limited to the examined set; 25 unexamined candidates remain unknown, not absent.
Declared sensitivity counts remain labeled alternatives to the corrected 20/14/5 counts.

what-the-seal-proves.heading: What does a receipt actually prove?
what-the-seal-proves.synopsis: Two byte-different receipts can share a canonical digest. Inspect what a verifying seal binds, and why it cannot establish safety or authorization.
limits: This toy example measures no deployed receipt system or Ghost-Ark canonicalizer or corpus.
The film uses its own canonicalizer; it does not build on the lab repository, whose reuse licence is unstated.
Canonicalizer collisions are shown as possible, not prevalent.
Verifier acceptance establishes no semantic safety, authorization, or correctness.

same-scores__social-square.synopsis: A square cut of the same constructed shared-miss example.
limits: The 100 items and their arrangements are constructions, not measurements of a system.
The interval does not recover the true relationship between real guards or certify a stack as safe.
The independence point is one assumption's selection, not an identified answer inside the interval.

the-multiplication.synopsis: A short insert isolating the independence assumption behind multiplying individual miss rates.
limits: This illustration shows no measured system, deployment risk estimate, or test of independence.

the-stack.synopsis: A second visual construction of fixed individual misses and changing overlap, with both guards evaluated on all items.
limits: The items and arrangements are constructions, not measurements of a system.
Both guards must be evaluated on the same full set. Sequential routing, where a guard never sees blocked items, is a different quantity.
The bounds do not recover the true relationship between real guards or certify a stack as safe.
The independence point selects one possible outcome under an assumption; the film does not identify an answer inside the interval.

the-missing-column-trailer.synopsis: A combined preview of the constructed example, bounded census, and selected released-file arithmetic.
limits: The constructed example shows possible shared misses; it measures no deployed system and does not certify safety.
The census covers its examined set. A missing reporting field proves neither poor performance nor universal absence.
The released-file counts describe one selected subset under unstated vendor settings, not a population rate or product ranking.
A stack interpretation requires common full exposure and fixed thresholds. Exclusive coverage does not establish causal contribution or all overlaps.

the-falsifier-that-fired.synopsis: A missed qualifying source changed the census. Follow the rejected count, preserved history, and corrected result.
limits: The corrected bounded census does not establish exhaustive coverage or universal absence.
A missing reporting field does not show poor guardrail or stack performance.
Sensitivity counts remain declared alternatives, never replacements for the corrected 20/14/5 counts.
The correction process is not claimed to be novel or a standard.

the-correction-invitation.synopsis: The route for challenging the record with a checkable source.
limits: This invitation records no submitted correction and does not guarantee that every challenge is valid.
